question.text: Where in Oregon do you need a valid driving privilege to drive a motor vehicle?

answer.text: In Oregon you need a valid driving privilege to drive a motor vehicle on highways and on premises that are open to the public.

teaching.text: The privilege rule reaches beyond highways: any premises open to the public, like a public parking lot, also requires a valid driving privilege. Remember: public roads need a privilege.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In Oregon you need a valid driving privilege to drive a motor vehicle on highways and on premises that are open to the public.

question.text: Which kind of driving privilege does the Oregon Driver Manual cover?

answer.text: The Oregon Driver Manual covers only what is needed to obtain a Class C non-commercial driving privilege.

teaching.text: The manual is focused on one goal, the Class C non-commercial privilege, which is the ordinary passenger car license. Remember: Class C only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Oregon Driver Manual covers only what is needed to obtain a Class C non-commercial driving privilege.

question.text: Does the Oregon Driver Manual cover commercial license requirements?

answer.text: The manual addresses only the Class C non-commercial driving privilege, so commercial license requirements are outside its scope.

teaching.text: Commercial license requirements are outside this manual, which addresses only the Class C non-commercial privilege. Remember: commercial is elsewhere.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual addresses only the Class C non-commercial driving privilege, so commercial license requirements are outside its scope.

question.text: What does Oregon DMV test for an original driving privilege?

answer.text: For an original driving privilege, Oregon DMV tests three things: your vision, your knowledge of driving, and your driving skill.

teaching.text: A first Oregon privilege means three separate checks: how well you see, what you know about driving, and how well you actually drive. Remember: eyes, mind, hands.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For an original driving privilege, Oregon DMV tests three things: your vision, your knowledge of driving, and your driving skill.

question.text: What must you do and show before each DMV test?

answer.text: Before each test you must pay the test fee and show proof of your identity, your date of birth and your current home address.

teaching.text: Every test starts with paperwork: the test fee plus proof of who you are, when you were born and where you live now. Remember: fee plus three proofs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before each test you must pay the test fee and show proof of your identity, your date of birth and your current home address.

question.text: How is the test fee paid, and where can you usually test?

answer.text: The test fee is paid on its own, separately from any other fee you owe DMV, and most DMV offices can give the tests.

teaching.text: The test fee is never folded into another DMV bill, and you can take the tests at most DMV offices. Remember: fee stands alone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The test fee is paid on its own, separately from any other fee you owe DMV, and most DMV offices can give the tests.

question.text: What permit rule applies to an applicant under eighteen seeking a driver license?

answer.text: An applicant under eighteen who is applying for a driver license must have held a permit for at least six months.

teaching.text: Applicants under eighteen seeking a driver license must have held a permit for six months or more. Remember: six months on permit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant under eighteen who is applying for a driver license must have held a permit for at least six months.

question.text: Does the six-month permit-holding rule apply to adult applicants?

answer.text: The six-month permit-holding rule applies to applicants under eighteen who are seeking a driver license, not to adult applicants.

teaching.text: The six-month permit rule is for applicants under eighteen seeking a driver license, and adult applicants are not bound by it. Remember: permit clock is for minors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The six-month permit-holding rule applies to applicants under eighteen who are seeking a driver license, not to adult applicants.

question.text: What happens to your privilege if you wear glasses or contacts for the vision test?

answer.text: If you wear glasses or contact lenses for the vision test, your driving privilege will show that you must drive with corrective lenses.

teaching.text: Testing with glasses or contacts means your privilege will require you to wear them whenever you drive. Remember: lenses in, lenses always.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you wear glasses or contact lenses for the vision test, your driving privilege will show that you must drive with corrective lenses.

question.text: Does wearing glasses or contacts for the vision test mean you fail?

answer.text: Wearing glasses or contacts for the vision test does not fail you; it adds a corrective-lens requirement to your driving privilege.

teaching.text: Testing with lenses is not a failure; it adds a corrective-lens requirement to your privilege. Remember: lenses restrict, never fail.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wearing glasses or contacts for the vision test does not fail you; it adds a corrective-lens requirement to your driving privilege.

question.text: What does the vision test cost, and what happens if you fail it?

answer.text: The vision test is free, and an applicant who fails it is handed a form to take to a licensed vision specialist.

teaching.text: The vision test costs nothing, and someone who fails it leaves with a form for a licensed vision specialist. Remember: free test, specialist form.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The vision test is free, and an applicant who fails it is handed a form to take to a licensed vision specialist.

question.text: How is the vision test different from the other tests in cost and outcome?

answer.text: Unlike the other tests, the vision test carries no fee, and failing it leads to a referral form for a licensed vision specialist rather than an automatic denial.

teaching.text: The vision test is the free one, and failing it brings a referral form for a licensed vision specialist rather than an automatic denial. Remember: free, then referral.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unlike the other tests, the vision test carries no fee, and failing it leads to a referral form for a licensed vision specialist rather than an automatic denial.

question.text: What does the Class C knowledge test cover, and what is the manual meant to contain?

answer.text: The Class C knowledge test covers road signs, traffic laws and other things a driver must know, and the manual is meant to contain everything needed to pass it.

teaching.text: The knowledge test draws on road signs, traffic laws and other driver know-how, and the manual is written to hold all of that material. Remember: signs, laws, know-how.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Class C knowledge test covers road signs, traffic laws and other things a driver must know, and the manual is meant to contain everything needed to pass it.

question.text: How many questions does the Class C knowledge test have, and how many correct answers pass it?

answer.text: The Class C knowledge test has thirty-five multiple-choice questions, and you pass by answering twenty-eight of them correctly.

teaching.text: The Class C knowledge test asks thirty five multiple-choice questions, and the passing standard is twenty eight correct answers. Remember: thirty five asked, twenty eight right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Class C knowledge test has thirty-five multiple-choice questions, and you pass by answering twenty-eight of them correctly.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: thirty five asked, twenty eight right

question.text: Where and when can you take the knowledge test?

answer.text: You can take the knowledge test online through DMV2U at any hour, or at a DMV office either as a walk-in on standby or by appointment.

teaching.text: You choose where to take the knowledge test: online through DMV two U at any hour, or at an office on standby or by appointment. Remember: online anytime or office.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You can take the knowledge test online through DMV2U at any hour, or at a DMV office either as a walk-in on standby or by appointment.

question.text: Who is allowed in an office knowledge-test area?

answer.text: In an office testing area, only the people being tested and authorized translators are allowed.

teaching.text: The office testing area is closed to everyone except the people testing and authorized translators. Remember: test takers and translators.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In an office testing area, only the people being tested and authorized translators are allowed.

question.text: Where may a translator go during testing, and where may they never go?

answer.text: At an office, authorized translators may enter the knowledge-test area, whereas a translator is never allowed inside the car during the drive test.

teaching.text: Authorized translators may join you in the knowledge-test area, but they are never allowed in the car for the drive test. Remember: translator in room, not car.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At an office, authorized translators may enter the knowledge-test area, whereas a translator is never allowed inside the car during the drive test.

question.text: What format and language options does an office knowledge test offer?

answer.text: Office knowledge tests run on a touch-screen monitor, come in several languages with or without audio, and you may bring your own earbuds or headphones.

teaching.text: Office knowledge tests run on a touch screen, come in several languages, can include audio, and you may bring your own earbuds. Remember: touch screen, many languages.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Office knowledge tests run on a touch-screen monitor, come in several languages with or without audio, and you may bring your own earbuds or headphones.

question.text: Which aids are banned during the knowledge test, and which one may be allowed?

answer.text: During the test you may not use a DMV manual, notes or electronic devices, though a paper foreign-language translation dictionary is allowed with permission.

teaching.text: No DMV manual, notes or electronic devices are allowed, but a paper translation dictionary can be used if permission is given. Remember: paper dictionary, with permission.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During the test you may not use a DMV manual, notes or electronic devices, though a paper foreign-language translation dictionary is allowed with permission.

question.text: Which aid may be used during an office knowledge test only with permission?

answer.text: A paper foreign-language translation dictionary may be used during an office knowledge test only with permission, while a DMV manual, notes and electronic devices are never allowed.

teaching.text: Only one aid can be approved during an office test, a paper translation dictionary, while manuals, notes and devices stay banned. Remember: dictionary asks, notes never.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A paper foreign-language translation dictionary may be used during an office knowledge test only with permission, while a DMV manual, notes and electronic devices are never allowed.

question.text: Which behaviors count as cheating on the knowledge test?

answer.text: Talking, writing or taking notes, using a cell phone or any electronic device, or having someone else test for you all count as cheating.

teaching.text: Cheating covers talking, writing or taking notes, using a phone or other device, and letting someone else test in your place. Remember: talk, write, phone, stand-in.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Talking, writing or taking notes, using a cell phone or any electronic device, or having someone else test for you all count as cheating.

question.text: Who should an applicant contact about a special accommodation for the knowledge test?

answer.text: Applicants who need a special accommodation for the knowledge test should contact their local DMV office.

teaching.text: If you need a special accommodation to take the knowledge test, reach out to your local DMV office. Remember: ask your local office.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants who need a special accommodation for the knowledge test should contact their local DMV office.

question.text: What happens to someone caught cheating on the knowledge test?

answer.text: Anyone caught cheating fails the knowledge test and must wait ninety days before testing again.

teaching.text: A cheater does not just lose points: the test is failed and a ninety day wait follows before any retest. Remember: cheat means ninety days.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anyone caught cheating fails the knowledge test and must wait ninety days before testing again.

question.text: After failing a knowledge test at an office, can you retest the same day?

answer.text: After failing a knowledge test at an office you may be able to retest the same day, depending on how much testing capacity that office has.

teaching.text: After an ordinary office failure, a same-day retest is possible only when that office has enough testing capacity. Remember: same day if capacity.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After failing a knowledge test at an office you may be able to retest the same day, depending on how much testing capacity that office has.

question.text: How does the reason you failed change when you can retake the knowledge test?

answer.text: Retest timing depends on why you failed: an ordinary office failure may allow a same-day retest if the office has capacity, but a cheating failure bars any retest for ninety days.

teaching.text: The reason for failing sets the wait: an ordinary office failure may retest the same day, but cheating locks you out for ninety days. Remember: cheating closes the door.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Retest timing depends on why you failed: an ordinary office failure may allow a same-day retest if the office has capacity, but a cheating failure bars any retest for ninety days.

question.text: What equipment does the online knowledge test require, and what cannot be used?

answer.text: The online knowledge test requires a desktop or laptop with a keyboard, mouse and webcam; phones, tablets and other touchscreen devices cannot be used.

teaching.text: Online testing needs a desktop or laptop with a keyboard, mouse and webcam, and touchscreen devices like phones and tablets are not allowed. Remember: laptop yes, phone no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The online knowledge test requires a desktop or laptop with a keyboard, mouse and webcam; phones, tablets and other touchscreen devices cannot be used.

question.text: How does the device for the online knowledge test differ from the office test?

answer.text: The online knowledge test must be taken on a desktop or laptop with keyboard, mouse and webcam, unlike the office test, which is given on a DMV touch-screen monitor.

teaching.text: The online test runs on your own desktop or laptop, while the office test runs on a DMV touch-screen monitor. Remember: home computer, office touchscreen.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The online knowledge test must be taken on a desktop or laptop with keyboard, mouse and webcam, unlike the office test, which is given on a DMV touch-screen monitor.

question.text: What does the webcam do during the online knowledge test?

answer.text: The webcam takes a clear photo of you when the online test starts and random photos during it to confirm who is taking the test.

teaching.text: The webcam photographs you as the online test begins and at random moments during it, so DMV can confirm who is testing. Remember: camera confirms who tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The webcam takes a clear photo of you when the online test starts and random photos during it to confirm who is taking the test.

question.text: What supervision rule applies to online test takers under eighteen?

answer.text: An online test taker under eighteen must be supervised by a proctor who is over twenty-one, and one proctor may supervise no more than two tests in any twenty-four-hour period.

teaching.text: Online test takers under eighteen need a proctor over twenty one, and each proctor is limited to two tests in a twenty four hour period. Remember: proctor over twenty one.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An online test taker under eighteen must be supervised by a proctor who is over twenty-one, and one proctor may supervise no more than two tests in any twenty-four-hour period.

question.text: Whose age does each part of the online proctor rule describe?

answer.text: The proctor rule applies only to online test takers under eighteen, and the proctor must be over twenty-one, not merely a licensed adult of any age.

teaching.text: Under eighteen describes the online test taker who needs a proctor, and over twenty one describes the proctor, not just any licensed adult. Remember: minor tests, adult watches.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The proctor rule applies only to online test takers under eighteen, and the proctor must be over twenty-one, not merely a licensed adult of any age.

question.text: How many times may you take the knowledge test online?

answer.text: Online, you may test twice within a twenty-four-hour period and four times in total; after the fourth attempt you must test at a DMV office.

teaching.text: Online you get two attempts within a day and four in all, and after the fourth you must test at an office. Remember: two a day, four total.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Online, you may test twice within a twenty-four-hour period and four times in total; after the fourth attempt you must test at a DMV office.

question.text: How do online knowledge-test retest limits differ from office retests?

answer.text: Online retests are capped differently from office retests: online you get two tries per twenty-four hours and four in all before you must go to an office.

teaching.text: Office retests depend on capacity, but online retests are counted: two per day and four total before an office visit. Remember: online retests are counted.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Online retests are capped differently from office retests: online you get two tries per twenty-four hours and four in all before you must go to an office.

question.text: What does the drive test check, and what does the examiner do?

answer.text: The drive test checks turning, backing, parking, lane changes, speed control, signaling, vehicle control and general driving ability, with the examiner in the front seat giving directions and reviewing the results with you afterward.

teaching.text: The drive test covers turning, backing, parking, lane changes, speed, signaling and control, with the examiner directing you from the front seat and reviewing results after. Remember: examiner rides up front.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The drive test checks turning, backing, parking, lane changes, speed control, signaling, vehicle control and general driving ability, with the examiner in the front seat giving directions and reviewing the results with you afterward.

question.text: When may DMV waive the drive test for a new resident?

answer.text: DMV may waive the drive test for a new resident who surrenders an out-of-state license that is valid or has been expired for less than one year.

teaching.text: A new resident can have the drive test waived by surrendering an out-of-state license that is valid or expired less than a year. Remember: surrender a recent license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: DMV may waive the drive test for a new resident who surrenders an out-of-state license that is valid or has been expired for less than one year.

question.text: What must a new resident's out-of-state license be for a drive test waiver?

answer.text: A drive test waiver for a new resident needs an out-of-state license that is still valid or expired less than one year, and that license is surrendered.

teaching.text: The new-resident waiver works only with an out-of-state license still valid or expired under one year, and you hand that license over. Remember: valid or under a year.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A drive test waiver for a new resident needs an out-of-state license that is still valid or expired less than one year, and that license is surrendered.

question.text: How can driver education lead to a drive test waiver?

answer.text: DMV may also waive the drive test when it receives proof that you finished an ODOT-Approved Driver Education Course within the past two years.

teaching.text: Proof of an ODOT-Approved Driver Education Course finished within the past two years may lead DMV to waive the drive test. Remember: approved course, two years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: DMV may also waive the drive test when it receives proof that you finished an ODOT-Approved Driver Education Course within the past two years.

question.text: What does a driver education waiver of the drive test require?

answer.text: A drive test waiver based on driver education needs proof of an ODOT-Approved course completed within the past two years.

teaching.text: The driver education waiver looks back two years and requires proof of an ODOT-Approved course. Remember: course within two years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A drive test waiver based on driver education needs proof of an ODOT-Approved course completed within the past two years.

question.text: How are drive tests scheduled, and what must the vehicle have?

answer.text: Drive tests are by appointment only, and you must bring a passenger vehicle with current registration and valid proof of insurance, or the test is rescheduled.

teaching.text: Drive tests require an appointment and a passenger vehicle with current registration and valid insurance proof, otherwise the test is rescheduled. Remember: appointment, registration, insurance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drive tests are by appointment only, and you must bring a passenger vehicle with current registration and valid proof of insurance, or the test is rescheduled.

question.text: Who may ride in the vehicle during the drive test?

answer.text: Only you and the examiner may ride in the vehicle during the drive test, so translators, family, friends and pets must stay out.

teaching.text: During the drive test, the car holds only you and the examiner, so translators, family, friends and pets wait outside. Remember: just you and examiner.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only you and the examiner may ride in the vehicle during the drive test, so translators, family, friends and pets must stay out.

question.text: How should you prepare the vehicle's interior before the drive test?

answer.text: Before the drive test, remove any weapons from the vehicle, switch off electronics such as the radio and your phone, and clear objects off the dashboard and rearview mirror.

teaching.text: Get the car ready before the test: take out any weapons, turn off the radio and phone, and clear the dashboard and rearview mirror. Remember: no weapons, clear dashboard.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before the drive test, remove any weapons from the vehicle, switch off electronics such as the radio and your phone, and clear objects off the dashboard and rearview mirror.

question.text: How soon can you retake a failed drive test?

answer.text: After failing a drive test you must wait until the next business day to take it again.

teaching.text: A failed drive test cannot be retaken until the next business day. Remember: next business day.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After failing a drive test you must wait until the next business day to take it again.

question.text: Can a failed drive test be retaken the same day?

answer.text: A failed drive test cannot be retaken the same day; the earliest retake is the next business day.

teaching.text: Unlike an office knowledge test, a failed drive test never gets a same-day retake; the next business day is the earliest. Remember: drive retest waits a day.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A failed drive test cannot be retaken the same day; the earliest retake is the next business day.

question.text: How do you book a drive test, and how far ahead does DMV suggest booking?

answer.text: Drive test appointments are made through DMV2U or by calling five hundred three-nine hundred forty-five-five thousand, and DMV suggests booking at least three weeks before the date you want.

teaching.text: Book the drive test through DMV two U or by phone, and DMV suggests doing it at least three weeks before your preferred date. Remember: book three weeks ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drive test appointments are made through DMV2U or by calling five hundred three-nine hundred forty-five-five thousand, and DMV suggests booking at least three weeks before the date you want.

question.text: What can a certified Third Party drive tester offer, and what is the tradeoff?

answer.text: A certified Third Party drive tester may offer quicker appointments or times DMV does not, but the cost of testing can be higher.

teaching.text: A certified Third Party tester may get you an earlier slot or a time DMV does not offer, though the price can be higher. Remember: faster, maybe pricier.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A certified Third Party drive tester may offer quicker appointments or times DMV does not, but the cost of testing can be higher.

question.text: How does booking a Third Party Tester compare with testing at DMV?

answer.text: Booking through a certified Third Party Tester can be faster or offer extra days and times, but it may cost more than testing at DMV.

teaching.text: A Third Party Tester trades speed and extra appointment times for a cost that may be higher than testing at DMV. Remember: more times, maybe more cost.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Booking through a certified Third Party Tester can be faster or offer extra days and times, but it may cost more than testing at DMV.

question.text: What happens if the test vehicle fails the examiner's check?

answer.text: The examiner checks the test vehicle first, and a vehicle that fails the equipment check means the drive test must be rescheduled.

teaching.text: The examiner inspects the car before you drive, and if it fails that inspection, the drive test gets a new date. Remember: car fails, test moves.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The examiner checks the test vehicle first, and a vehicle that fails the equipment check means the drive test must be rescheduled.

question.text: Which two problems unrelated to your driving force a rescheduled drive test?

answer.text: Missing proof of insurance and a failed vehicle equipment check both force a rescheduled drive test, even though neither involves your driving.

teaching.text: Missing insurance proof and a failed equipment check both push the drive test to a new date, even though neither is about your driving. Remember: paper or parts, rescheduled.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Missing proof of insurance and a failed vehicle equipment check both force a rescheduled drive test, even though neither involves your driving.

question.text: Which basic equipment must the test vehicle have working?

answer.text: The test vehicle must start on its own power and have working front and rear turn signals, brake lights, a horn, seatbelts and tires that are not bald or damaged.

teaching.text: The test car must start on its own and have working turn signals front and rear, brake lights, a horn, seatbelts and sound tires. Remember: start, signal, stop, honk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The test vehicle must start on its own power and have working front and rear turn signals, brake lights, a horn, seatbelts and tires that are not bald or damaged.

question.text: What must be true of the passenger door, passenger seat and muffler?

answer.text: The passenger door must open and close with its handle from both inside and outside, the passenger seat must be proper, secure and reasonably clean, and the muffler must not leak excessively or make unreasonable noise.

teaching.text: The passenger door handle must work from inside and outside, the passenger seat must be secure and reasonably clean, and the muffler reasonably quiet. Remember: door, seat, quiet muffler.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The passenger door must open and close with its handle from both inside and outside, the passenger seat must be proper, secure and reasonably clean, and the muffler must not leak excessively or make unreasonable noise.

question.text: What must the test vehicle display, and what views must it give?

answer.text: The test vehicle must display valid registration, have side view or rearview mirrors, and give both the driver and the examiner a clear view to the front, sides and rear.

teaching.text: The car must show valid registration, have side or rearview mirrors, and let both the driver and the examiner see clearly all around. Remember: registration, mirrors, clear views.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The test vehicle must display valid registration, have side view or rearview mirrors, and give both the driver and the examiner a clear view to the front, sides and rear.

question.text: Which equipment does the test vehicle need when the weather calls for it?

answer.text: When the weather calls for them, the test vehicle also needs traction tires or chains, windshield wipers, headlights, taillights and a window defroster.

teaching.text: Bad weather adds requirements: traction tires or chains, wipers, headlights, taillights and a defroster. Remember: weather adds the extras.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When the weather calls for them, the test vehicle also needs traction tires or chains, windshield wipers, headlights, taillights and a window defroster.

question.text: When are chains, wipers, headlights, taillights and a defroster required on the test vehicle?

answer.text: Traction tires or chains, wipers, headlights, taillights and a defroster are required on the test vehicle only when the weather calls for them, unlike the always-required items such as brake lights and a horn.

teaching.text: Chains, wipers, headlights, taillights and a defroster depend on the weather, while brake lights and the horn are always required. Remember: weather decides the extras.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traction tires or chains, wipers, headlights, taillights and a defroster are required on the test vehicle only when the weather calls for them, unlike the always-required items such as brake lights and a horn.
